subject: research/robofab-solreftimestep
professional: a robotics simulation researcher who tunes MuJoCo contact for grasping (soft-constraint model, solref/solimp/refsafe, noslip, impratio); first checks: does the numbers rerun, is the refsafe reading right, and is 'fails' a loss of grip or an artefact of the pass/fail criterion (does the outcome depend on force, threshold and run length)

evidence.correctness: Numbers reproduce and the arithmetic and the refsafe reading are right; what 'fails' means is the problem (see claims, domain). (1) Installed mujoco 3.16.0 (the README's version) into /usr/bin/python3.13 and re-ran `cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/091d6275-30d5-5492-8889-4ef9ed0beb80/scratchpad/robofab/copy && /usr/bin/python3.13 experiments/run.py` (6.4 s): results.txt byte-identical to the committed one; figure.py regenerates an identical SVG. (2) Analytic bound by hand: cover = 40 x 30 x 4 mm = 4800 mm^3 x 1240 kg/m^3 = 5.952 g; m(g+a)/(2 mu) = 5.952e-3 x 409.81 / 1.0 = 2.4392 N and x 809.81 = 4.8200 N, matching results.txt. (3) The refsafe clamp max(solref, 2 dt), which the README says it took from the docs and did not test, checked in MuJoCo: refsafe on, a=400, 1.3 x bound: worst displacement is identical to 6 digits for (solref 0.2, dt 0.2) and (0.4, 0.2) = 1.795248 mm and for (0.1, 0.15) and (0.3, 0.15) = 1.346584 mm; with refsafe disabled the dt >= 0.2 ms cells blow up (QACC NaN warnings, 1.8 to 33 m displacement). (4) 'none' really means no tested force holds: holds() is false at 1.02, 1.05, 1.1, 1.3, 2, 4, 8 and 12.4 x bound in 8 'none' cells (monotone.py), so the bisection's single check at 60 N does not mislabel cells.
evidence.completeness: Claimed and checked: '6 tests, < 1 s' (6 passed in 0.42 s with pytest; unittest command also valid); 'about 6 s' (6.4 s); grid 3 x 4 x 2 = 24 cells and 6 holding (counted in results.txt); ladder 8 timesteps x 3 pairs with effective-constant lines (present); '6 of 6 cells in the two 800 rows with dt >= 0.15 ms fail' (true); figure regenerates from results.txt. No stubs or TODOs. All Next steps (refsafe off, solimp, cause of non-monotonicity, other six parts) are open, and are stated as open.
evidence.verification: `cd research/robofab-solreftimestep && /usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`: 6 passed in 0.42 s (after `pip install mujoco==3.16.0`; mujoco is not declared in pyproject.toml). min_force(), which produces every number in results.txt, has no test at all. Four mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 survived (hold threshold x1.5 at sim.py:66; min_force returning the failing bracket `lo` instead of `hi` at sim.py:80; side-load doubled in moving_bound at model.py:74), 1 caught (carrier velocity not prescribed at sim.py:62, 2 tests fail). A changed slip criterion or a bisection that returns the wrong end leave the suite green.
evidence.craft: Read model.py, sim.py, run.py, figure.py, the test file. Short and readable. Defects: sim.py and model.py are verbatim copies of research/robofab-solrefmap (`diff -q` silent), one of 49 robofab-* slugs, so a fix must be repeated; pyproject.toml declares no dependencies (mujoco, numpy); run.py:32-33 and :52-53 write results with open() never closed and write the files twice; the carrier is moved kinematically by overwriting qpos/qvel before each mj_step (sim.py:61-63) rather than with a mocap/weld or actuator, the harness candidate the README itself suspects; holds() reports only a bool, discarding the displacement that decides the result.
evidence.claims: Disclaimers present: 'stylised' (title, page x10), 'Produced with AI assistance', 'Simulation only', a Limitations section that names the 2 mm criterion and the 0.05 s window; the served page https://marisstella.app/research/robofab-solreftimestep/ returns 200. The literal numbers are backed by results.txt. But the framing outruns the files: the title asks what 'breaks a moving grasp', and 'no force up to 60 N holds' reads as loss of grip, while 13 of the 15 failing ladder cells are a force-independent creep of 2.14 to 3.59 mm along the load at 10 x the friction bound (identical at 2 x and 10 x; impratio 1, 10, 100 changes nothing), crossing the fixed 2 mm threshold; only the dt = 0.4 ms cells at 800 m/s^2 (220 mm) and the solref 0.5 ms cells (224 mm, pads lose the part) are gross slip. The 'practical consequence' (solref 0.1 ms held at 800 m/s^2 for dt <= 0.1 ms) does not survive a longer move: with t_acc = 0.2 s instead of 0.05 s, min_force at (800, 0.1 ms, 0.05 ms) returns None. 'The held cells form a window' is a smooth displacement curve minimised where 2 dt = solref (1.80 mm at dt = 0.1 for solref 0.2) crossing 2 mm, not a holding window.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun everything in 6 s with a pip install, and the refsafe clamp observation is correct and useful (I confirmed it in MuJoCo in seconds; the README deferred that test). But the binary outcome hides the mechanism the README calls unexplained: per-cell displacement at fixed force (ladder.py) gives 3.58, 1.80, 1.35, 1.85, 2.14, 2.34, 2.49, 2.59 mm (a=400, solref 0.3) and 219.9, 3.59, 2.69, 1.80, 2.39, 2.79, 3.09, 3.29 mm (a=800, solref 0.2) across dt 0.4 to 0.025 ms: a continuous creep that grows as dt falls below solref/2 and grows with run length. With a 3 mm threshold the a=800, solref 0.2 row would hold at four timesteps, not one. A researcher would need to redo the study with displacement (or creep rate) as the outcome. Nearest prior work, none cited: MuJoCo documentation, Computation/Soft constraints and the solref/refsafe/noslip options; Todorov (2014) ICRA 'Convex and analytically-invertible dynamics with contacts and constraints' (the soft-contact model that permits creep); Erez, Tassa and Todorov (2015) ICRA, simulator comparison including grasp stability. Novelty: the refsafe clamp is documented behaviour; the creep-vs-dt curve could be a modest new observation but is not reported. One micro-question per slug, contrary to the programme model in research/CLAUDE.md.
evidence.domain: Against MuJoCo contact-tuning practice: (a) the outcome is a binary 2 mm threshold over a fixed 0.05 s window, while soft constraints are known to permit force-independent creep, so the right measure is displacement or creep rate vs (solref, dt), not a min-force bisection whose ratio is ~1.01 wherever it 'holds'; (b) the refsafe clamp is a single option flag and was not tested (it takes one line, mjDSBL_REFSAFE); (c) impratio, the usual knob for slip with elliptic cones, was not considered (it has no effect here, which is itself diagnostic: the creep is not friction-cone slip); (d) the carrier is teleported each step, the README's own candidate cause, not checked against a mocap or actuated carrier; (e) single part, single run length. The README states (a)'s criterion and (b) as limits, which keeps it honest, but a senior practitioner would not sign off 'timestep can make it worse' or the solref 0.1 ms recommendation from this method.

defects.what: The headline outcome ('fails', 'breaks a moving grasp', 'no force up to 60 N holds') is a fixed 2 mm threshold on a force-independent creep, not loss of grip: 13 of 15 failing ladder cells creep 2.14-3.59 mm at 10 x the friction bound (same at 2 x; impratio has no effect) while contact is kept. The 'window' and 'a finer timestep can make it worse' are a smooth displacement curve, minimised at 2 dt = solref, crossing 2 mm; a 3 mm threshold would flip 3 of 7 failing cells in the a=800, solref 0.2 row.

The practical recommendation (solref 0.1 ms holds at 800 m/s^2 for dt <= 0.1 ms) depends on the 0.05 s acceleration window: with t_acc = 0.2 s min_force at (800, 0.1 ms, 0.05 ms) returns None, because the creep grows with run length. A practitioner tuning a workcell twin for a longer move would act on it and see the same 'failure'.

min_force (the bisection that produces every reported ratio) has no test; mutants returning the failing bracket, loosening the 2 mm criterion by 50%, or doubling the side load all leave the 6 tests green.

The refsafe explanation is left untested though it is a one-flag check (mjDSBL_REFSAFE); it holds (identical trajectories for equal max(solref, 2 dt)), so the README undersells a confirmable result and leaves an open caveat that need not be there. holds() also discards the displacement, so no continuous outcome is reported.

No prior work on MuJoCo soft-contact creep or contact-parameter tuning cited (MuJoCo docs on soft constraints/refsafe/noslip; Todorov 2014 ICRA; Erez, Tassa and Todorov 2015 ICRA); refs.bib holds only the MuJoCo paper and Zykov 2005.
pyproject.toml declares no dependencies; mujoco and numpy must be installed by hand for the tests to import.
sim.py and model.py are verbatim copies of research/robofab-solrefmap (one of 49 robofab-* slugs); results files are written twice with open() never closed.

verdict: A small, honest-in-its-limits MuJoCo grid that reruns byte-identically in 6 s with mujoco 3.16.0; the analytic bound (2.4392 / 4.8200 N) is right, and the refsafe clamp the README took from the docs is confirmed (equal max(solref, 2 dt) gives identical trajectories). It misses the bar on claims and verification. The binary 'holds within 2 mm over 0.05 s' outcome hides that 13 of 15 failing ladder cells are a force-independent 2.1-3.6 mm creep with contact kept, so the 'window' and 'finer timestep can make it worse' are a smooth creep curve (minimum at 2 dt = solref) crossing an arbitrary threshold, and the recommended solref 0.1 ms setting fails at any force once the move lasts 0.2 s. min_force, which produces every number, is untested (3 of 4 seeded bugs survive). Reporting displacement or creep rate instead of a threshold would turn this into a usable result.
